subject: IAM traceback, account-ownership map and SCIM change-log request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <security@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: audit@cloudops-consulting.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: IAM traceback, account-ownership map and SCIM change-log request

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Quick heads up from the GreenLine side: after our last bulk provisioning window (Mar 15 delta job) we observed a cluster of duplicated accounts and a handful of service accounts that appear to have been orphaned from their owners. The audit team has flagged this as a potential break in our least-privilege attestation and we need a set of artifacts to close the loop for our SOC 2 evidence pack.

From Redwood we need the following by COB (your timezone) next Wednesday (Mar 24):
- SCIM delta job logs (Mar 15, 03:00-06:00 UTC) including the attribute changes and error rows (redacted to preserve PII if needed).
- Account ownership map (owner uid -> account list) as of Mar 15 and a snapshot as of today.
- A short narrative explaining the delta job behavior that could cause duplicates (2–3 bullets).
- SSO assertion samples (SAML Response) for two affected users (redacted except for NameID and attributes).
- RBAC role snapshot and the role-to-permission mapping for the affected groups.

We can share this with our auditor (cc'd) once received. If you foresee any blockers or need us to accept redacted artifacts in a secure shared location, please propose a plan.

Appreciate quick confirmation that this is possible — the auditor is expecting an ETA by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Maya R. Singh
Director, Information Security
GreenLine Health

[Attachment: incident-ref-GL-2027-03.txt (text/plain)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <security@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, audit@cloudops-consulting.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IAM traceback, account-ownership map and SCIM change-log request

Maya — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the artifacts you asked for; below is a proposed mutual action plan so expectations are aligned:

Mutual Action Plan (MAP)
- Today (Mar 22): Redwood confirms scope and delivers a redaction plan + secure share location. (Owner: Karthik)
- Tue, Mar 23 EOD: Initial artifacts delivered (SCIM delta logs, ownership map, RBAC snapshot). (Owner: Laura)
- Wed, Mar 24: SSO assertion samples delivered in separate, encrypted transfer (Owner: Markus).
- Thu, Mar 25: Joint call to review artifacts and close any auditor questions (30 min).

We will use a shared, permissioned drive under HS-47923 (we can redacted PII in logs; alternatively we can provide line-level redaction and a verifier hash). Please confirm which option your auditor prefers.

I will kick off the collection now — Laura will produce the ownership matrix and RBAC export, and Markus will extract SAML assertion samples with minimal PII.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Note: I have flagged this thread as priority and created an internal ticket SEC-782 for tracking.]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <security@greenlinehealth.com>, audit@cloudops-consulting.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IAM traceback, account-ownership map and SCIM change-log request

Hi Maya / Audit team —

Attached are the initial artifacts as discussed: ownership-matrix.xlsx (owner UID, account IDs, creation_ts, last_login_ts, current_status) and scim-delta-sample.csv (first 500 rows of the Mar 15 delta job; PII redacted).

Root-cause summary (short):
- The Mar 15 delta job normalized the email attribute during an intermediate transformation step; a subset of accounts had both email and login attributes set differently which caused the import to create new accounts instead of matching existing ones.
- The normalization rule was introduced during a schema alignment change on Mar 14; we missed a small subset that used a legacy login attribute.
- We have since run a de-duplication pass and created a temporary mapping table to merge duplicates; owner confirmation remains pending for ~12 accounts.

Remediation and next steps:
- We will provide the RBAC snapshot (roles_export.json) and the role-permission matrix by EOD today.
- Markus will extract two SAML Response samples and deliver them via an encrypted link tomorrow (Mar 24) to satisfy auditor requirements.
- We will list the 12 pending owner confirmations and propose the owner verification query for your acceptance.

Attachments:
- [Attachment: ownership-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
- [Attachment: scim-delta-sample.csv (text/csv)]

If the auditor needs full unredacted logs, we can stage them in a restricted drive (HS-47923) and provide access to an appointed verifier. Let us know the preference.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura / Karthik / Markus —

Thanks for the quick turn here. I confirm receipt of ownership-matrix.xlsx and the SCIM sample rows. The auditor (cc) is happy to accept redacted logs staged in the restricted drive HS-47923 for verification.

Two asks before the call on Thu: 
1) Please include a short column in the ownership matrix called 'merge_action' indicating whether the account was merged, disabled, or requires owner-confirmation.
2) For the SSO assertion samples, please ensure NameID is included and all other attributes are minimal — the auditor only needs attribute names and values hashes for validation.

If you can drop the updated matrix and the encrypted link to the SAML samples by EOD today, we can keep the Thu call to 11:00 AM and close out the evidence collection.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Director, Information Security
GreenLine Health
